responsibilities: Design and develop data models and database architecture specifically tailored for marketing data analytics and reporting within a data warehousing environment
Work closely with marketing teams to understand their data needs and translate business requirements into technical specifications
Implement and maintain scalable and efficient data warehouses and data marts that support various marketing functions, including campaign management, customer segmentation, and ROI analysis
Optimize data flows and architecture to improve data accuracy, accessibility, and quality, ensuring data is available for real-time and batch processing
Develop and enforce best practices and standards for data modeling, data extraction, and data loading into the data warehouse
Collaborate with IT and business stakeholders to ensure that the data architecture supports the goals of the marketing team while aligning with the overall business strategy
Prepare and maintain documentation of data architectures, configurations, and processes
Stay up-to-date with industry trends and advancements in data warehousing and marketing technologies to continuously improve the data infrastructure

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Develop and enforce best practices and standards for data modeling, data extraction, and data loading into the data warehouse
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Accuracy, quality, enforced standards and data privacy compliance carry the posting; "fast-paced environment" appears once in a project-management requirement.
evidence.domain_risk: Experience with data security (including PHI and PII), as well as data privacy regulations (CCPA and GDPR)
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: The architecture handles PHI and PII under CCPA and GDPR, so a design error carries regulatory exposure.
evidence.collaboration_width: marketing teams; IT; data scientists; analysts
evidence.data_team_maturity: We are looking for a skilled and experienced Marketing Data Architect to join our Enterprise Data Warehousing Team.
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: An Enterprise Data Warehousing Team with a Sr. Manager of Data & Analytics, running warehouses, lakehouses and integrated data stores at scale.
evidence.jd_authorship: Implement and maintain scalable and efficient data warehouses and data marts that support various marketing functions, including campaign management, customer segmentation, and ROI analysis
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: The marketing use cases are named, but the rest of the section is generic architecture language with all the specificity sitting in the requirements list.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: Work closely with marketing teams to understand their data needs and translate business requirements into technical specifications
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The role exists to serve marketing — campaign management, segmentation, attribution and ROI analysis.
evidence.autonomy_level: Develop and enforce best practices and standards for data modeling, data extraction, and data loading into the data warehouse
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: Setting and enforcing standards is directive, but the role is an individual contributor translating marketing requirements into specifications.
evidence.ai_role: Experience with analytics techniques using ML and AI to assist data scientists and analysts in deriving insights from data
evidence.ai_role_explanation: The architecture is expected to align with organizational AI/ML goals and serve data scientists — the AI runs downstream of what this role builds.
evidence.testing_framing: Optimize data flows and architecture to improve data accuracy, accessibility, and quality, ensuring data is available for real-time and batch processing
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Improving data accuracy and quality is a responsibility the candidate owns, though no testing framework is named.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: Experience with data security (including PHI and PII), as well as data privacy regulations (CCPA and GDPR)
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Privacy compliance appears once, in requirements, while the responsibilities themselves are framed around delivery and enablement.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: designing, developing, and maintaining the data architecture specifically for marketing analytics and insights
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: Designing new marketing data models sits alongside maintaining and continuously improving an existing warehouse estate.
evidence.work_arrangement: Hybrid: Employee divides their time between in-office and remote work. Access to an office location is required. (Frequency: Minimum 2 days per week; may vary by team but will be weekly in-office expectation)
evidence.loss_aversion: "Experience with data security (including PHI and PII), as well as data privacy regulations (CCPA and GDPR)" — regulated personal data is explicitly in scope for the architecture.
